name: Cultuurhuis Bergeijk
known: The house is named for the Van Daalen family: Roelof van Daalen, co-director of the weaving firm De Ploeg, commissioned it (tour page).
Board, all unpaid: Anja Tils (chair), Anneke Schellens, Christine van den Berghe, Huub Gijsbers and Jos Smeets; over 40 volunteers; a cultural ANBI (Cultuurhuis site).

name: Van Abbemuseum
known: Founded by the cigar businessman Henri van Abbe, who sold his collection to the Eindhoven city council in 1934 (Wikipedia).
Defne Ayas was announced as director from 15 September 2025 (Wikipedia).
History: the founder was a cigar businessman (Wikipedia); no page shows that the family business funds the museum today.

name: Groninger Museum
known: Run since 2025 by artistic director Roos Gortzak.
Nynke Stellingsma has been interim general administrator since the business director left on 1 January 2026 (Dutch Wikipedia).

name: Fries Museum
known: Director Kris Callens left in February 2025; the museum cited transgressive behaviour.

name: Museum De Lakenhal
known: The director is Tanja Elstgeest and the museum had 29,281 visitors in 2021, a year affected by Covid-19 lockdowns (Wikipedia).

name: Bonnefanten
known: Directors: Alexander van Grevenstein from 1986, Stijn Huijts from 2012 (Wikipedia).
Top salaries: the director earned €192,605 and the business director €166,098; supervisory board members are unpaid (2025 annual report).
Board: Petra Stienen (chair), Lieve Schouterden, Bastiaan Klomp, Britte Sloothaak, Madeleine van Lennep, Maurice Lambriex, Barbara Strating.

name: Marres, House for Contemporary Culture
known: Run by a supervisory board and a managing director appointed in 2013 on a permanent contract (annual report 2022).
The 2022 supervisory board was Nelleke Barning (chair), Roberto Lanckohr (vice chair), Noor van Putte, Laurie Cluitmans, Hans Bongartz and Arsine Nazarian.
Chair and vice chair swapped roles on 1 January 2023 (annual report 2022).

name: Vleeshal Center for Contemporary Art
known: Vivian Ziherl became managing director in September 2025, after an interim directorship by Julia Mullié from February 2025.

name: Kröller-Müller Museum
known: Founded by the collector Helene Kröller-Müller, who gave her whole collection to the Dutch state in 1935.
Named for its founder, Helene Kröller-Müller.
Helene Kröller-Müller Fund: founded in 2013, it has contributed more than €2 million in total to educational projects, conservation work and exhibitions (the museum).

Governance: supervisory board of Herman Dijkhuizen (chair), Henriette Bast, Fried van 't Hof, Wim Pijbes and Marije Hulshof; director Benno Tempel; about 115 employees (the museum's organisation page).

name: Chabot Museum
known: It was founded by Martijn van der Vorm, whose death NOS reported on 29 April 2026; the family wealth rests on the Holland America Line, sold in 1989 (NOS).
The report says the museum depends on the city and the company of its private founders; no reporting found of that company's name or payments.

name: Kijk-Kubus
known: The museum site names Ed R. de Graaf as founder of the show cube and says it "opens its door this year for the 42nd season", with no year given.
Site names founder Ed R. de Graaf.
